# Criteria fixtures

Real, captured JUnit XML samples from the four test runners P-B1's confirmation
logic must parse. Each sample has one passing test, one failing test, and one
skipped test, so `confirm.mjs` can be tested against every status this spec
defines (`pass`, `fail`, `unconfirmed`). None is hand-written; each was
generated by actually running the named tool.

| File                              | Tool            | Version           | Captured with                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vitest-4.1.5.junit.xml`          | Vitest          | 4.1.5             | `npx vitest run --reporter=junit --outputFile=<path>` on a 3-test file (`describe > it` names)                      |
| `pytest-9.1.1.junit.xml`          | pytest          | 9.1.1             | `pytest --junit-xml=<path> -o junit_family=xunit2` on a 4-test file (pass, fail, an uncaught exception, and a skip) |
| `go-junit-report-2.1.0.junit.xml` | go-junit-report | v2.1.0-dev (HEAD) | `go test -v ./...` piped into `go-junit-report` on a 3-test file                                                    |
| `bats-core-1.13.0.junit.xml`      | bats-core       | 1.13.0            | `bats --formatter junit <file>` (the version vendored in `node_modules/bats`) on a 3-test file                      |

Notes for the parser and its tests:

- pytest reports an uncaught exception as `<failure>`, not `<error>` — §5's rule ("a JUnit testcase for a named test with a `failure` or `error` child" is `fail`) already covers both, so this is a real-world case the parser must not special-case away.
- Vitest's test name is `"<describe> > <it>"`; bats-core's and go-junit-report's names have no `>` separator. The confirmation rule (KD-3, §4) must match a name that equals or ends with the criterion's test name after any of `>`, `::`, `.`, `/`.
- bats-core's failure text is plain content, XML-entity-encoded where needed (e.g. `&#39;` for an apostrophe) — not a `CDATA` section. go-junit-report uses `CDATA`. The parser must handle both.
